dedupe_keys.name: arkema crosby organic peroxide fires after hurricane harvey flooding csb report 2017 08 i tx

description: The federal investigation of a chemical plant failure caused by hurricane flooding. The CSB report of May 2018 says the Arkema plant at Crosby, Texas, lies in the 100-year and 500-year floodplain; Harvey's rainfall in August 2017 exceeded equipment design elevations, and the plant lost power, backup power and refrigeration for organic peroxides, so products were moved into refrigerated trailers and staff evacuated. On 31 August 2017 peroxides in a trailer decomposed and burned; 21 people sought medical attention after fumes crossed a highway kept open inside the 1.5-mile evacuation zone, and over three fires more than 350,000 pounds of peroxide burned, keeping over 200 residents from home for a week. Key issues named are site flood vulnerability, flood risk assessment, flood resilience and emergency response. The 154-page report is a free download. Coverage is one plant. Caveats: the licence is not stated on the page read. For simulation it is a worked natech chain from flood to power loss to fire. A related catalogue record is the eNATECH accident database.
